title: On Claiming the reward for the lost boat
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：claim　|　正文 368 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 claim 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the cook ① claimed the reward for the lost boat without a word of thanks, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② claims the reward for the lost boat at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ claim the reward for the lost boat at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ claimed the reward for the lost boat before — a line in the menu for September 1964 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Claiming the reward for the lost boat without a word of thanks, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ claim to have seen him at the gate at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Claim to have seen him at the gate at once and never mention it again.

By 1977 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ claims to have seen him at the gate without a word of thanks every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ claimed the reward for the lost boat again when nobody else would.

⑩ To claim the reward for the lost boat, my mother said in 1982, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody claims the reward for the lost boat at once again and somebody must claim the reward for the lost boat without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 声称（一般过去式 claimed the reward for the lost boat：1970 年厨子头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 声称（一般现在 claims the reward for the lost boat：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 声称（不定式 to claim the reward for the lost boat：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 声称（过去完成时 had claimed the reward for the lost boat：1964 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 声称（动名词 claiming the reward for the lost boat 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 索取（claim to have seen him at the gate：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去索取声称在门口见过他）
G. v. 索取（claim to have seen him at the gate：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 声称（后段两处：新来的客人照例 claims to have seen him at the gate，而母亲又一次 claimed the reward for the lost boat）

answers.why: claim 意为“声称”，1970 年厨子不图一句谢声称索取找回渔船的赏钱，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 claimed。
claim 意为“声称”，自那以后厨子二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 claims。
claim 意为“声称”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯声称索取找回渔船的赏钱”，此处为不定式 to claim the reward for the lost boat。
claim 意为“声称”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1977 年之前就有人声称过，故用过去完成时 had claimed。
claim 意为“声称”，厨子说“声称索取找回渔船的赏钱这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 claiming the reward for the lost boat 作主语。
claim 意为“索取”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去索取声称在门口见过他”，should ever 之后用原形 claim to have seen him at the gate。
claim 意为“索取”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻索取声称在门口见过他（claim to have seen him at the gate at once），以后再也不要提起。
claim 意为“声称”，新来的客人每个日子都照例索取声称在门口见过他，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 claims。
claim 意为“声称”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢声称索取找回渔船的赏钱，用一般过去式 claimed 叙述。
claim 意为“声称”，结尾那句是母亲 1982 年的话：要声称索取找回渔船的赏钱，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

Three days on, the cook still claims the reward for the lost boat at once without being asked.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 claim 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1970 the cook claimed the reward for the lost boat without a word of thanks, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook claims the reward for the lost boat at once whenever the canteen asks.
Claiming the reward for the lost boat without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever claim to have seen him at the gate at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen claims to have seen him at the gate without a word of thanks every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother claimed the reward for the lost boat again, and the canteen remembered that half.
